questions.statement: What is the most appropriate formal greeting when meeting a teacher in the morning?
questions.context: Two students, Mateo and Valentina, meet on their first day at a public school in Bogotá.

Correct! This is a polite and formal greeting for the morning.

The student needs to identify the correct formal greeting for a morning school context. "Good morning" is the standard formal greeting for this time of day.

questions.statement: Why does Andrés say "Welcome to Colombia"?
questions.context:
A dialogue between a tourist and a local guide in Cartagena.
Guide: "Good afternoon! Are you Mr. Miller?"
Tourist: "Yes, I am. Nice to meet you."
Guide: "Welcome to Colombia. I am your guide, Andrés."

options.text: Because he is asking for the tourist's name.
options.feedback: Incorrect. He already knows the name.

options.text: Because he wants to know where Mr. Miller is from.
options.feedback: Incorrect. This is a welcoming phrase, not a question.

options.text: Because he is receiving a visitor in his country.
options.feedback: Correct! "Welcome" is used to greet someone arriving at a place.

options.text: Because he is saying goodbye to the tourist.
options.feedback: Incorrect. They are just meeting for the first time.

questions.explanation:
The student analyzes the social function of the word "Welcome" within a specific communicative context.

questions.statement: Choose the sentence that is grammatically perfect and natural for a profile.
questions.context: A profile description on a student social network.

options.text: I have 14 years and I live in Manizales.
options.feedback: Incorrect. In English, we use "be" for age, not "have".

options.text: I am 14 years old and I live in Manizales.
options.feedback: Correct! This follows the correct structure for age and residence.

options.text: I am 14 years and I lives in Manizales.
options.feedback: Incorrect. "Lives" is third person; the first person is "live".

options.text: I is 14 years old and I live in Manizales.
options.feedback: Incorrect. "I is" is grammatically wrong.

questions.explanation:
The student analyzes and compares different structures to identify the correct way to express age and location in English.

questions.statement: Which of the following summaries best describes Diana?
questions.context:
A short text about a student.
"Hello! I am Diana. I am a student at a school in Bucaramanga. I am 13. My favorite subject is Science. I want to be a doctor."

options.text: She is a 13-year-old girl who lives in Bucaramanga and likes doctors.
options.feedback: Incorrect. She wants to be a doctor, not just "likes" them.

options.text: Diana is a student who lives in Bucaramanga and her favorite subject is English.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Her favorite subject is Science.

options.text: Diana is a 13-year-old student from Bucaramanga who dreams of being a doctor.
options.feedback: Correct! This accurately summarizes her age, location, and aspiration.

options.text: Diana is a doctor who works in a school in Bucaramanga.
options.feedback: Incorrect. She is a student, not a doctor yet.

questions.explanation: The student must evaluate the information provided in the text and select the summary that most accurately represents the facts and intentions mentioned.
